focus.jnote: The backdrop is still near records — but the risk clock is loud this morning. The S&P 500 eased ~0.06% Tuesday to ~7,753 as fading U.S.–Iran deal hopes pushed oil up and weighed on sentiment; the Nasdaq slipped ~0.32% to ~26,605 and the Dow eased to ~53,976. This morning futures are fractionally higher, helped by upbeat tech earnings — CoreWeave jumped ~18% and Super Micro ~9% after their prints. The overnight story is still oil: WTI ~$84, Brent ~$89, with Iran keeping its Strait-of-Hormuz reopening conditions hard and a reported tanker incident in the Bab el-Mandeb. That feeds straight into inflation fear right as July CPI prints today at 8:30 AM ET (consensus 3.4% YoY, core 2.5%) and PPI drops Thursday. The VIX is still low near ~15.5 but ticking up, and the 10Y sits near ~4.7%.
focus.notdown: Energy stays the day’s clearest structural bid as crude holds ~$84 on the Hormuz breakdown — but the entire move is a war/supply premium, a two-sided trade, not a clean Sniper bid. The scanner did NOT board any energy single-name today. On the earnings side, HRB (H&R Block) boarded as a Type A bull-put on its post-earnings gap — but its reaction-day relative volume printed far below the confirmation bar, so treat it as unconfirmed until 9:35 ET.
focus.notup: No clean bearish single-name boarded this morning. Fuel-sensitive cyclicals (airlines, transports) are pressured by the crude spike, and long-duration tech is exposed if CPI runs hot on top of the oil move — but selling bear calls into a low-VIX, record-adjacent tape minutes before CPI carries squeeze risk on any benign print or de-escalation headline. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new until the print clears.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite is 53 (WARM) and P(≥1% gap) is ~35% (right on the 35% trigger) — already elevated. More decisively, CPI prints this morning inside hours, which under the rules cannot be GREEN and defaults to YELLOW. Stack on the still-hot oil premium (WTI ~$84, Brent ~$89) and an open-ended Hormuz tail, and the honest stance is: half size, A-grade only, keep DTE short enough to clear CPI/PPI or simply wait for the prints to pass, and validate every chain at 9:35 ET — especially HRB, whose reaction volume was below the bar.

setups.read: H&R Block (HRB) is a Type A post-earnings gap — it reported Q4 FY26 after the close Tuesday, beating EPS at $2.38 (est ~$2.21–2.31, a ~6.5% beat) on revenue ~$1.14B (roughly in line, a slim ~1.4% surprise). The scanner tags it a double beat and gapped it up hard — prior close $46.67, pre-market print near ~$52, an ~11.7% move versus a ~7% implied. Earnings risk is now behind it (next print ~Nov 5–10, well outside DTE), liquidity passed (ATM spread $0.05, OI 545), and there are no S/R layers within 7% of price. Two honest concerns to carry into the open: (1) reaction-day relative volume printed ~0.02x — far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, so the gap is NOT volume-confirmed and could be a thin, gappy quote; and (2) the whole tape is on hold for the 8:30 CPI print. Grade is A+ per the scanner, but confirm the volume and a real two-sided market before doing anything.
setups.check_note: Volume is the gate — reaction rel-vol ~0.02x is well below the 1.3x bar, so the gap is unconfirmed; require real volume AND a tight two-sided chain at 9:35 or SKIP. Require price > the $46.67 prior close AND > today’s open, upper third of range. With NO S/R layers between price and the short strike and CPI printing at 8:30, quarter-to-half size at most and keep DTE clear of CPI/PPI.
